transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, doctor. Yeah, thanks. Um, well, I guess I came in because... man, it's just been a really weird couple of weeks. 

I work surveillance, you know, security over at the casino. Lots of graveyard shifts, sitting in a dark room staring at camera feeds for eight to ten hours straight. Usually, when I get off a shift, I am just absolutely starving. I have this whole routine where I stop at the diner on the way home and get a big plate of eggs and hash browns, or at least grab a couple of those heavy breakfast burritos from the corner spot if I'm too beat to sit down anywhere. 

But lately... I'd say for the last few weeks, I’ve barely had an appetite at all. It's like my stomach is just completely turned off. I'll get my usual food, the stuff I usually really look forward to after a long night of watching the tables, and it just sits there. I end up just staring at it. I try to force down a few bites because I know I need the fuel, especially with my crazy schedule, but it's just... I don't know, it's a chore. It's like chewing cardboard. My buddy in the monitor room even noticed I stopped bringing my usual snacks in. I just have no interest in eating, which is really not like me at all, and it's starting to weird me out.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight or how much you're eating overall, and has this affected how you sleep?

Weight? Um... you know, I haven't actually stepped on a scale in... man, I couldn't even tell you how long. I have one of those old dial ones in the bathroom, not the fancy digital ones everybody has now, but honestly, I just use it to prop the door open when it gets too steamy after a shower, so I couldn't give you an actual number. My uniform belt feels about the same, I guess? Maybe a little loose on the third notch, but the casino issues us these really cheap synthetic leather belts that stretch out after a couple of months anyway, so it's hard to judge by that. I'm definitely eating way less overall, like I was saying. Just... skipping meals entirely sometimes because I just can't be bothered to force it down. 

But as for sleep... man, sleep is always such a weird thing for me anyway. When you work the graveyard shift, you're trying to get some shut-eye when the sun is just blasting outside, right? I bought these heavy, thick blackout curtains off the internet a couple years ago, but light still manages to leak in around the edges, especially in the summer. So my sleep is always a little all over the place just by the nature of the job. I can't say I've noticed the food thing affecting it, though. I'm not waking up starving or with stomach pangs or anything like that. I just get home, try to wind down, and get into bed around 9 AM like always. I don't think I'm sleeping any differently than usual, honestly. I haven't really paid much attention to it, to be perfectly honest with you, but nothing jumps out at me. It's really just the eating that's completely out of whack right now.
Have you noticed that things you usually enjoy, like your favorite foods or maybe even your downtime after work, don’t seem to give you the same satisfaction they used to?

Yeah, actually, now that you mention it... it's not just the food. It's kind of bleeding into everything else, too. Like, I usually have this whole routine to keep myself sane with the graveyard hours, you know? I used to really look forward to my morning runs—well, morning for everyone else, right before I go to sleep for me. It was the perfect way to burn off the weird energy from sitting in that dark surveillance room all night, watching people at the tables. But lately, I just look at my running shoes sitting by the door and I just walk right past them. 

And my guitar, too. I’ve got this old Fender Stratocaster I bought at a pawn shop off the strip a few years back. I used to plug it in, throw on my heavy headphones so I don't wake the neighbors since I'm awake at such weird hours, and just jam out for an hour or two on my days off. It was my absolute favorite way to unwind and get out of my own head. But now... I don't know, it's just sitting there on the stand gathering dust. I look at it and I just can't get myself to care enough to even pick it up. 

Same goes for cooking dinner. I used to love taking my time on a Tuesday night, chopping stuff up, making a real meal from scratch instead of just eating that heavy diner food. Now, the thought of getting the pans out and standing at the stove just feels like this massive chore. I keep skipping all of it—the runs, the guitar, the cooking. It’s like all the stuff I used to actually enjoy doing just feels like a heavy obligation now, like a checklist of chores, and I just can't bring myself to care about any of it anymore.
Have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for the past few weeks?

Yeah, I guess "down" is one way to put it. But it’s more like... I don't know, most days I feel like I’m just carrying this really heavy, flat feeling around with me everywhere I go. It's hard to explain, but it's like... okay, take the break room at the casino, right? It's this windowless little room right down the hall from the monitor bank. Got a couple of noisy vending machines, terrible fluorescent lights, and usually a few of the other security guys are in there shooting the breeze, complaining about management or talking about some guy they had to escort off the floor for getting too rowdy at the craps table. I usually jump right into the conversation, but for the last few weeks, I’ll just be sitting in there with my coffee and I’m just... I'm not really there. It's like I'm watching them on one of my surveillance feeds instead of actually being in the room with them. Just totally detached and flat. 

And it's the exact same thing when I'm home, too. I'll be sitting on the couch on my day off, and my family is right there in the living room with me, just going about their day, talking, doing whatever... and I should be engaged, you know? I should be present. I want to be present. But I just feel so weighed down by this... this emptiness. It’s not like I’m sitting around crying or anything dramatic like you see on TV, it’s just this heavy, dull feeling that never really lifts, almost every single day from the minute I wake up. I hear my family talking to me, but I'm just completely zoned out, like a ghost in my own house. It's just a really heavy way to get through the day.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or have other people said you seem slowed down, or on the flip side, have you felt restless or unable to sit still?

Well, yeah, actually... it's funny you bring that up, because it's not even just me noticing it, it's the guys at work, too. I mean, I try to keep it together, you know? I really do. But we have these shift briefings right before we take over the monitor room—usually around 11:30 PM, right before the graveyard shift officially starts. The shift supervisor, usually this guy Mike, he goes over whatever happened during swing shift, who to look out for, if there are any high rollers coming in that we need to keep a special eye on, that sort of thing. It's usually pretty fast-paced, a lot of back-and-forth, guys asking questions, throwing out jokes, just getting ready for the night. 

But lately... I don't know, it's like I'm moving through molasses. Mike will ask me a direct question about, say, camera coverage on pit three, and I swear, I hear the question, I know the answer, but it takes me... I don't know, it feels like an eternity just to get my mouth to form the words. And it's not just my speech, either. It's my whole body. Like, when we're all standing around the briefing table and then it's time to head out to the surveillance room, everybody else just grabs their clipboards and goes, and I'm still just... slowly standing up, taking an extra second to grab my radio, just moving so deliberately slow. 

A couple of the guys have even commented on it. My buddy Dave, he works the cameras right next to me, he pulled me aside the other night and was like, "Hey man, you good? You're moving like you're underwater tonight." And he's right, that's exactly what it feels like. It's like my brain is sending the signal to move or speak, but the message gets delayed somewhere along the line. I'm just a full step behind everybody else in the room, both physically and... I guess verbally, too. It's really frustrating because I want to snap out of it and just be my normal self, but I just can't seem to get my gears to turn any faster. So, no, I'm definitely not restless... it's completely the opposite. Just... heavy and slow.
